messages.subject: First online GGIR user-meeting on the 10th of September 2019
messages.subject_clean: First online GGIR user-meeting on the 10th of September 2019
messages.body_plain:
Dear GGIR users,

I would like to invite you to our first online GGIR-user meeting.

When:
10th of September 2019 at 5pm CEST, 4pm BST, 11am EST, and 8am PDT. Sorry to all eastern users, next time I will pick a time that is more convenient for you.

Aim:
Discuss with you as users what improvements to GGIR are desirable and how we can realize them. The online GitHub issue-tracker <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/issues> and GGIR Google group <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!forum/RpackageGGIR> provide some ideas, but it does not tell me which idea is most urgent or who can participate in realizing them via committing time or financial support.

Agenda:
Brief overview by me on current and planned GGIR developments.
Series of 3 minute pitches by GGIR users about what they would like to see improved + 2 minutes for questions.
Plenary discussion to assess priority of ideas and how we can follow-up on the suggested improvements. This does not necessarily have to involve my consulting services, external contributions are also welcome. It is open source software after all and software becomes stronger if it has multiple contributors.
Closing remarks and opportunity for feedback on the format of this meeting.
If you would like to take part in the meeting then please e-mail me and tell me:
Your name and affiliation.
Whether you would like to pitch an idea for improving GGIR and what that idea is.
Whether you are working on a GGIR enhancement yourself and would like to pitch this.
If you are interested but cannot attend the proposed time and date then please also let me know.

The meeting will take place via video conference (Zoom), and you will receive a personal meeting invitation for it. The duration of the meeting will depend on the number of pitch proposals I receive, but will not last more than 90 minutes. I will record the meeting, and will put it up online afterwards. Attendance is for free.

Best regards,
Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
www.movementdata.nl <http://www.movementdata.nl>

messages.subject: Processing multiple .bin files in a folder
messages.subject_clean: Processing multiple .bin files in a folder
messages.body_plain:
Hello GGIR group,

Our team has been having a bit of difficulty with processing multiple .bin files at once in GGIR, and I was hoping to clarify some parts of the script to see if we have this right:

After setting the working directory to the parent folder, we have moved all the .bin files into a folder named "all_files", and subsequently set our datadir to "all_files" (see entire script below).

Is this the best way to do this to automatically process multiple files in sequence - and is there a maximum number of .bin files that can be processed?

Thanks in advance for your help!

Very best,
Lydia

Our GGIR script:

# NOT RUN {
mode= c(1:5)
datadir= "all_files"
outputdir= "all_results"
desiredtz="America/Toronto"
studyname="DEW"
f0 = 1
f1 = 2

g.shell.GGIR(#-------------------------------
             # General parameters
             #-------------------------------
             mode=mode,
             datadir=datadir,
             outputdir=outputdir,
             studyname=studyname,
             f0=f0,
             f1=f1,
             overwrite = TRUE,
             do.imp=TRUE,
             idloc=1,
             print.filename=FALSE,
             storefolderstructure = FALSE,
             #-------------------------------

             # Part 1 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             windowsizes = c(5,900,3600),
             do.cal=TRUE,
             do.enmo = TRUE,
             do.anglez=TRUE,
             chunksize=1,
             printsummary=TRUE,
             desiredtz= "America/Toronto",
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 2 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             strategy = 1,
             ndayswindow=7,
             hrs.del.start = 1,
             hrs.del.end = 1,
             maxdur = 35,
             includedaycrit = 16,
             L5M5window = c(0,24),
             M5L5res = 10,
             winhr = c(5,10),
             qlevels = c(c(1380/1440),c(1410/1440)),
             qwindow=c(0,24),
             ilevels = c(seq(0,400,by=50),8000),
             mvpathreshold =c(100,120),
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 3 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             timethreshold= c(5,10),
             anglethreshold=5,
             ignorenonwear = TRUE,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 4 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             includenightcrit = 16,
             def.noc.sleep = c(),
             loglocation= c(),
             outliers.only = FALSE,
             criterror = 4,
             relyonsleeplog = FALSE,
             sleeplogidnum = TRUE,
             colid=1,
             coln1=2,
             do.visual = TRUE,
             nnights = 35,
             #-------------------------------
             # Part 5 parameters:
             #-------------------------------
             # Key functions: Merging physical activity with sleep analyses
             threshold.lig = c(40),
             threshold.mod = c(100),
             threshold.vig = c(400),
             excludefirstlast = FALSE,
             boutcriter = 0.8,
             boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
             boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
             boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
             boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
             boutdur.lig = c(1,5,10),
             boutdur.mvpa = c(1,5,10),
             timewindow = c("WW"),
             #-----------------------------------
             # Report generation
             #-------------------------------
             do.report=c(2,4,5),
             visualreport=TRUE, dofirstpage=TRUE,
             viewingwindow = 1)
## End(Not run)

messages.subject: Problems in Part 1 with GENEActiv .csv files
messages.subject_clean: Problems in Part 1 with GENEActiv .csv files
messages.body_plain:
Hi Vincent and all,

I'm using GGIR to process GENEActiv .csv files and I haven't been able to get Part 1 to go past reading the first file name. I'm aware that the GENEActiv .bin files are meant to be used in GGIR (and that the .csv files should work in theory), however the trial manager said they only have the .csv files. I've used GGIR in the past for Actigraph .csv files and have found the data so useful, so I'm determined to find a way to make GGIR work for these data as well.

My specific question is whether 1) the .csv file needs to be altered in some way before running it through GGIR, 2) the .csv file needs to be converted to a .bin file (through R somehow?) first, or 3) there's any special code that needs to be put into GGIR to help it recognise this file type?

If it's useful, the specific error message that comes up in Part 1 is: Error in as.POSIXlt.character(as.character(x), ...) :
  character string is not in a standard unambiguous format

Thanks very much for any help you can offer!

Best wishes,
Janelle

messages.body_plain:
Hi Janelle,
I worked on facilitating GENEActiv csv a long time ago, but have worked little with it. So, I am not sure how well it still works.
You should not need to convert or adept it.

Please check that you are really looking at the raw data, and not at one of the epoch level aggregates that are also available for GENEActiv.

If the code is truly not suitable anymore for modern GENEActiv csv files then I am afraid that this will require a significant time investment from me.
I am happy to do that as a consultancy service, please contact me directly if you are interested.

Best wishes,

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
www.movementdata.nl <http://www.movementdata.nl>

messages.subject: Any volunteers to test upcoming GGIR feature? (parallel GGIR)
messages.subject_clean: Any volunteers to test upcoming GGIR feature? (parallel GGIR)
messages.body_plain:
I could use some testers for a new GGIR functionality I am working on.
This functionality will make GGIR parts 2, 3 and 5 able to process multiple files in parallel on any desktop/laptop machine with at least 4 CPU cores.

It seems to work on my laptop, but it would be great if others could also test it.

Instructions:

1. Install the development version of GGIR that has this new feature with the two lines of code below. Notice that you will also need to install R package "devtools" if you do not have it yet.

library(devtools)
install_github("wadpac/GGIR",ref="issue194_parallel")
2. Install R packages: "foreach" and "doParallel".
3. Re-start R(Studio)
4. Try to run your g.shell.GGIR call as you normally do for parts 2, 3 and 5 in a data sets of at least a dozen files.

If all goes well this should go (a lot) faster than before. How much faster depends on your machine. Please let me know if it generates any errors or if the speed does not go up.

I did not implement the parallel processing for parts 1 and 4 (yet), because for part 1 this is currently too tricky and for part 4 I think it is less relevant because part 4 is already fast.

Best wishes, Vincent

Hi Lydia,
Yes, this is how to do it.
Make sure outputdir is not a subfolder of datadir (In the upcoming GGIR version you will get a warning from GGIR if this is the case).
There is no maximum on the number of files.

Note that the data can be stored in subfolders of the directory specified by datadir, because GGIR searches for accelerometer files recursively. So, if there is a structure in your dataset you want to keep like research site, study stage, or year of data collection then this is possible. In that case you may want to consider argument 'storefolderstructure = TRUE' which will append your output csv files with a column specifying in what subfolder the data was found.

Best, Vincent

messages.subject: GGIR version 1.10-1 now online
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

GGIR version 1.10-1 is now available on CRAN, and the Windows binaries will be published in the upcoming 24 hours.

This release comes with a large number of upgrades, see full list here <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/news.html>.

The most important upgrades are:
- I have enabled multi-threading to make GGIR faster when you have at least 4 CPU cores.
- g.shell.GGIR now automatically creates a configuration file that records all argument setting used for in your analysis. Next, you can use this configuration file to share and replicate your analysis. Arguments supplied to g.shell.GGIR in addition to the configuration file will overrule whatever is in the configuration file. The configuration file is stored in the output folder and named config.csv.
- If you process part 1 after you have previously processed part 1 and 2 GGIR will automatically use the previously derived calibration coefficients and skip the auto-calibration procedure. This will speed up your analyses when you reprocess part 1.
- The default value for argument mode changed from c(1,2) to 1:5, whcih means that it does all five parts by default. I changed this because it seems logical that a naive user benefits from all parts of GGIR and not just part 1 and 2.
- Argument winhr can now be a vector with multiple values, e.g. c(3, 5, 6, 10), and with this part2 then calculates L3M3, L5M5, L6M6, L10M10 all in one go. Further, I have added an option (argument qM5L5) to extract percentiles (via R's quantile function) from the value distribution corresponding to these windows.

Finally a reminder that on the 10th of September I will be hosting a GGIR user meeting (online), see my email on the 2nd of August. If you want to take part then let me know.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
www.movementdata.nl <http://www.movementdata.nl>
